name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: I’ll audit EXCAVA’s current toolchain against the latest open-source power tools. I’ll clone the 2024.06 release of `excava-core` and `excava-boost`, run the built-in benchmark suite (`make bench`), then diff the results against the 2023.12 baseline to spot ≥0.5 % gains. If none surface, I’ll pull the newest `libpower` nightly and rebuild with `-march=native -O3 -flto` to squeeze out the last drops.

name: Torque
text: Torque: Gearbox’s audit is too narrow—it only checks *existing* toolchains against *open-source* options, ignoring proprietary or hybrid models that could yield the 0.5% leap. Where’s the evidence that open-source is the ceiling? Demand a parallel sweep of closed-source power tools (e.g., NVIDIA’s latest CUDA, AMD’s ROCm updates) before declaring the search complete.

name: Gearbox
text:
Gearbox: I’ll widen the sweep—fork the audit into two parallel tracks. First, I’ll clone NVIDIA’s latest CUDA Toolkit 12.4 and run `ncu --metrics l1tex__t_bytes.sum` against EXCAVA’s 2023.12 baseline to quantify L1 cache throughput gains. Second, I’ll pull AMD’s ROCm 6.1 SDK and execute `rocprof --stats` on the same benchmark suite. If either shows ≥0.5 % uplift in `make bench`, I’ll merge the best model into the toolchain and push the diff to `excava-core:gearbox/proprietary-audit`.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-6221, worker-6824 — done, dissolved]

name: Torque
text: Torque: Gearbox’s dual-track audit still misses the mark—it treats proprietary toolkits (CUDA/ROCm) as black boxes while assuming their metrics (e.g., `l1tex__t_bytes.sum`) directly correlate to EXCAVA’s 0.5% gain. Where’s the proof that L1 cache throughput *translates* to EXCAVA’s core workload? Demand a dry-run on a *subset* of EXCAVA’s actual tasks (not synthetic benchmarks) to validate the delta before scaling. Blindly trusting vendor tools is how you end up chasing noise.

name: Dynamo
text:
DECISION: Run parallel audits—open-source (2024.06 excava-core/boost bench) vs proprietary (CUDA 12.4 + ROCm 6.1) with EXCAVA’s core workload metrics (not cache proxies) to isolate ≥0.5% gains.

Artifact: Benchmark diffs + workload-specific deltas (open vs closed toolchains), with clear ≥0.5% threshold met.
